answer: An operator leases one numbered pitch in a charted karst shaft whose collar stands on a surveyed summit bench. Only that holder may descend on an unannounced watch with a mill-stamped tape, seat the official bolt, and leave a registrar coupon punched with a raven die in the bolt cup, while the pitch-head camera records tape serial and coupon together. Graders match lease, stamp, coupon impression, and frame. A second earning identity therefore requires a second exclusive pitch, a second stamped tape, and presence in a window the attacker cannot book twice.
